title: Administrator accounts and distribution
content: Administrators must collect assets, pay debts, and file accounts before distribution per the confirmed grant. Beneficiaries can demand accounts. Keep inventory, bank records, and the confirmation order.

title: Adopted children inheritance rights
citation: Law of Succession Act; Children Act
content: Legally adopted children inherit as children of the adopter with court orders as proof. Informal stays do not confer succession rights. Keep the adoption order and birth records.

title: Bank accounts of the deceased
citation: Law of Succession Act; banking practice guidance
content: Banks freeze accounts on notification of death and release funds to administrators with the grant. Small balances may have simplified procedures. Keep statements, IDs, and the death certificate.

title: Registering a caution on estate land
content: Beneficiaries fearing disposal can lodge cautions or restrictions at the registry pending succession. The caution warns buyers and requires court removal. Keep the caution receipt and succession filings.

title: Getting the chief's introduction letter
content: The chief lists the deceased, spouses, children, parents, and assets after verifying IDs and consulting family. Attend with IDs, death certificate, and asset documents. Keep the stamped letter and attendance notes.

title: Codicils: small changes to a will
content: Minor changes use a codicil executed with the same formalities as a will and read together with it. Store codicils with the original will. Keep a consolidated list of bequests for executors.

title: Customary land and succession consent
citation: Community Land Act, 2016; Law of Succession Act
content: Community and ancestral land succession needs community assembly consent in addition to court grants. Verify registration status with the community register. Keep consent minutes and grant copies.

title: Daughters equal inheritance rights
citation: Law of Succession Act; Constitution, Art. 27
content: Daughters inherit equally with sons; customary exclusion of daughters is unconstitutional. Challenge discriminatory distributions through objections and court. Keep heir lists and distribution proposals.

title: Death certificate for succession
citation: Births and Deaths Registration Act, Cap. 149
content: Succession cannot start without the death certificate from civil registration. Apply with burial permit and IDs. Keep several certified copies for banks, lands, and courts.

title: Settling estate debts before sharing
content: Loans, taxes, and funeral costs rank before beneficiaries. Administrators advertise for creditors and verify claims. Keep loan statements, demand letters, and payment records.

title: Widow eviction by in-laws: urgent action
citation: Law of Succession Act; Protection Against Domestic Violence Act
content: Evicting or dispossessing a widow without succession process is unlawful. Seek chief intervention, cautions at the lands registry, and urgent court orders. Keep marriage, death, and property documents.

title: Risks of handwritten DIY wills
content: Handwritten wills often fail on attestation, vague gifts, or missing residuary clauses. Have a lawyer review before signing. Keep drafts and the review notes.

title: E-filing succession causes
content: Succession causes are filed on the judiciary portal with petitions, chief letters, IDs, and asset lists. Pay assessed fees and track the case number. Keep digital receipts and stamped pleadings.

title: Terminal dues where an employee dies
content: Families claim unpaid salary, leave, and gratuity from the employer with death certificate and administrator letters. Demand an itemised statement. Keep payslips and payment records.

title: Choosing executors and trustees
content: Name trustworthy executors and alternates who can obtain probate, pay debts, and distribute. Brief them on asset locations and debts. Keep executor contacts with the will.

title: Assets abroad in Kenyan succession
citation: Law of Succession Act; private international law
content: Foreign property may need resealing or parallel proceedings where situated. Disclose all cross-border assets to the advocate. Keep foreign titles and grant copies.

title: Funeral expenses from the estate
content: Reasonable funeral and burial costs are paid from the estate with receipts. Disputes over extravagance are resolved by administrators and the court. Keep all expense receipts.

title: Naming guardians for minors in a will
citation: Law of Succession Act; Children Act, 2022
content: Wills should name guardians and trustees for minor children with maintenance directions. Courts prioritise the child's welfare in confirming arrangements. Keep guardian contacts updated.

title: Life insurance claims after death
content: Beneficiaries claim life cover with death certificate, policy, IDs, and claimant proof. Notify the insurer promptly. Keep policy documents and claim references.

title: Intermeddling with estate property is an offence
content: Selling, renting, or wasting estate property before a grant is intermeddling punishable by courts. Report to the chief, police, and succession court. Keep sale evidence and witness details.

title: Children shares in intestacy
content: Children share the intestate estate equally after the spouse's priority, including children born outside marriage who prove dependency. List every child to avoid later objections. Keep birth records.

title: Spouse share where there is no will
content: Surviving spouses take priority shares of intestate estates with children sharing the remainder per statutory tables. No distribution should occur before the grant. Keep the chief's letter and heir list.

title: Jointly owned property and survivorship
citation: Land Registration Act; Law of Succession Act
content: Joint tenancy may pass outside the will by survivorship while tenancy in common shares fall into the estate. Confirm the title type before drafting. Keep the title deed and search.

title: Legal aid for succession disputes
content: Indigent heirs facing dispossession can seek NLAS help with IDs, death certificate, and property documents. The toll-free line is 0800 720 640. Keep means and case documents ready.

title: Life interest for surviving spouses
content: Surviving spouses may hold life interests in the matrimonial home with remainder to children. The interest ends on remarriage in some cases. Keep the grant wording and property records.

title: Succession where a person is missing
citation: Law of Succession Act; presumption of death guidance
content: Estates of long-missing persons need presumption-of-death orders after police and gazette processes. Report the disappearance with OB records first. Keep search evidence and court orders.

title: Mobile money of a deceased person
content: Mobile money balances form part of the estate claimed with death certificate, administrator grant, and IDs. Report the death to the provider early. Keep transaction statements and claim references.

title: Muslim widow shares and iddah maintenance
citation: Islamic law of succession; Kadhi Courts Act
content: Muslim widows take fixed Quranic shares with iddah maintenance considerations through Kadhi courts. File with heir lists and property schedules. Keep marriage and death records.

title: NSSF survivor benefits
content: Survivors claim NSSF benefits with death certificate, claimant IDs, and relationship proof. File at the nearest branch with the member number. Keep claim receipts and correspondence.

title: Objecting to a succession grant
content: Interested persons may object within the gazette period or seek revocation for concealment. File affidavits with heir and asset evidence. Keep gazette copies and filing receipts.

title: Children born outside marriage in succession
citation: Law of Succession Act; Children Act
content: Children born outside marriage who were maintained or acknowledged rank as dependants with provision rights. Paternity evidence and maintenance proof matter. Keep support records and acknowledgements.

title: Parents and siblings where no spouse or child
content: Where the deceased left no spouse or child, parents and siblings take per statutory order. Distant relatives inherit only after closer classes. Keep family tree evidence and IDs.

title: Pension and gratuity on death
content: Death benefits follow scheme nomination forms and trust law, sometimes outside probate. Confirm nominees with the scheme. Keep nomination forms, IDs, and death certificates.

title: Distributing polygamous estates by house
content: Polygamous intestate estates are shared per house with the surviving spouses and children tables. Administrators map each house separately. Keep house lists and asset schedules.

title: Collecting rent from estate property
content: Rent from estate houses or land is estate income accounted by administrators, not personal income. Tenants should pay against receipts to the administrator. Keep tenancy and payment records.

title: Revoking a grant obtained by fraud
content: Grants obtained by hiding heirs or assets can be revoked with the distribution unwound. Apply with concealed-heir evidence. Keep the original filings and new proof.

title: SACCO shares on death of a member
content: SACCO deposits and shares pass to nominees or administrators with death certificate and grant. Guarantor liabilities attach first. Keep statements, nomination forms, and loan records.

title: Second wives and co-wives in succession
citation: Law of Succession Act; Marriage Act
content: Wives under valid customary or Islamic unions are spouses for succession alongside house-specific sharing. List each house with its children. Keep marriage evidence for every union.

title: Agreements to sell before grant are void
content: Purported sales of estate land before confirmation of grant pass no valid title. Buyers pay at their own risk. Verify the confirmed grant before paying for estate property.

title: SHIF dependant updates after death
content: Update SHIF records after a contributor dies so dependants retain correct cover. Carry the death certificate and household details. Keep updated registration slips.

title: Small estates and simplified process
citation: Law of Succession Act; magistrates jurisdiction
content: Lower-value estates may proceed in magistrates courts with simplified forms. Confirm the current jurisdictional threshold before filing. Keep valuations and asset lists.

title: Stepchildren and maintained dependants
content: Stepchildren maintained by the deceased may claim as dependants even without adoption. Maintenance evidence and household proof decide. Keep school fee and upkeep records.

title: Tax clearance for estates
content: Settle the deceased's tax arrears and obtain clearance before distributing business or rental estates. KRA may raise assessments on unreported income. Keep returns, assessments, and clearance letters.

title: Trusts for minor beneficiaries
citation: Law of Succession Act; Trustee Act
content: Shares for minors are administered in trust for school fees and upkeep until majority, with accounts to the court. Specify trustee powers and reporting. Keep trust accounts and receipts.

title: Formal requirements of a valid will
content: A will must be in writing, signed by the testator, and attested by two competent witnesses present together. Oral and unregistered informal wishes are hard to enforce. Store the original safely and tell executors where it is.

title: Revoking or changing a will
content: Revoke by a new will stating revocation, by codicil, or by deliberate destruction. Marriage can affect earlier wills, so review after life events. Keep every version dated with the latest clearly marked.

title: Storing wills and telling family
content: Keep the original will with an advocate or safe place and tell executors how to find it. Give copies to spouses without marking originals. Keep a one-page asset map with the will.

title: Who can witness a will
content: Witnesses should be adults of sound mind who are not beneficiaries, since gifts to attesting witnesses can fail. Each should sign in the presence of the testator. Keep witness IDs and contacts with the will.

title: Law of Succession Act — overview
content: The Law of Succession Act governs wills and administration of estates of deceased persons, including rights of surviving spouses, children, and dependants. Disputes are handled by the courts through probate or letters of administration. Keep the death certificate, will if any, and asset lists.

title: Chief's letter and beneficiaries — general guidance
content: Succession filings commonly require a chief's letter listing the deceased, spouses, children, and assets, plus IDs and death certificate. Ensure all beneficiaries are listed to avoid later objections. Keep copies of everything filed with the chief and court.

title: Confirmation of grant and distribution — general guidance
content: After a grant is issued, the court confirms it to approve how the estate will be shared among beneficiaries and dependants. No final distribution should occur before confirmation, and administrators must account for all property collected. Keep inventory records, consents, and the confirmation order.

title: Debts of the estate — general guidance
content: Debts of the deceased are settled from the estate before distribution, and creditors must prove their claims. Administrators should advertise for creditors where required and keep loan statements, demand letters, and payment records.

title: Dependant provision claims — general guidance
content: Spouses, children, and other dependants who were maintained by the deceased may apply for reasonable provision from the estate. Applications have strict time limits running from the grant, so seek advice early and keep proof of dependency and maintenance.

title: Applying for a grant and gazette objections — general guidance
content: Applications for grants of representation in Kenya are commonly gazetted so that interested persons can object or claim within the stated period. Applicants should give full and honest disclosure of heirs, assets, and liabilities from the start. Keep gazette notices, filed forms, and proof of service.

title: Intestate succession (no will) — general guidance
content: Where there is no valid will, the estate is distributed according to statutory shares for spouses, children, and other relatives. No one should subdivide or sell the deceased's land before lawful administration. A chief's letter and death certificate are usually required to start the process.

title: Deceased's land and cautions — general guidance
citation: Land Registration Act, 2012; Law of Succession Act
content: Land belonging to a deceased person should not be transferred until succession is completed and the grant confirmed. Beneficiaries fearing disposal may seek cautions or restrictions at the land registry and urgent court orders. Keep title deed copies, search results, and registry receipts.

title: Muslim intestate succession and Kadhi courts — general guidance
content: The estate of a deceased Muslim in Kenya is generally distributed according to Islamic law through the Kadhi courts or the High Court as appropriate. Heirs should identify all spouses, children, and dependants early to avoid later disputes. Keep death certificates, heir lists, and property documents.

title: Grant of probate and letters of administration — general guidance
content: Administrators must obtain a court grant before distributing an estate, then collect assets, pay debts and taxes, and distribute to beneficiaries with accounts. The process involves filing, gazette notice, and confirmation of the grant. Keep filing receipts, gazette copies, and bank records.

title: Wills — general guidance
content: A valid will must meet formal requirements including signature and witnesses, and testators should keep the original safely and tell executors where it is. Dependants left without reasonable provision may apply to court. Verify validity with a lawyer before acting.
